items.headline: Nvidia fell 2.9% to $150.96 on Nov 18 despite strong results and a raised growth outlook
items.why: When a beat plus higher guidance still sells off, the market is pricing leadership transition, export-restriction and regulatory risk above the earnings power of the AI-chip leader.

items.headline: Semiconductor index fell 17.1% in the week to Nov 20; Nvidia dropped 14% on Friday after a report of an SEC look at its accounting
items.why: The drop is concentrated in the stock that anchors the whole AI-capex trade, so a confirmed accounting problem would hit index funds and suppliers well beyond one company (the SEC report is relayed second-hand and not independently confirmed here).

items.headline: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $1.79B last week, the fourth straight week of net outflows
items.why: Four-week outflows of $4.34B show institutional demand, which drove the earlier rally, is now a source of selling pressure.

items.headline: Bitcoin traded near $62,300 after the Fed minutes, below its 200-week moving average near $68,000
items.why: A long-term average that previously acted as support is now overhead resistance, and a hawkish rate path is the backdrop for it (source is an automated market-analysis page).

sources.title: Fed Minutes Reveal Close Call on October Rates as December Hike Looms

items.headline: Fed minutes: almost all officials see further rate increases as likely; December hike priced near 90%
items.why: With the policy rate at 3.75-4% and tightening still the base case, rates are a headwind for equities and crypto rather than a tailwind.

sources.title: Fed minutes point to more rate increases as 10-year Treasury yield holds above 5%

items.headline: 10-year Treasury yield eased from about 5.07% on Nov 18 to roughly 4.92-4.95% by Nov 20-23
items.why: A pullback below 5% takes some pressure off valuations, but it came alongside the equity selloff, not from softer rate expectations.

items.headline: Gold fell about 9% last week, closing Friday at $3,526, then rebounded 2.3% to about $3,609-3,616 on Monday
items.why: Gold fell with equities instead of hedging them, a sign of forced selling and a stronger dollar, so its safe-haven role is not reliable in this stretch.

items.headline: Brent crude near $92 on Nov 23, down about 19% from $113.95 a month earlier
items.why: A fall of that size cuts the energy-driven inflation pressure behind the Fed's hawkish stance, but it is still 47% above a year ago.

items.headline: S&P 500 closed Nov 20 at 6,910.39, down 8.6% on the week and 11.6% below its October record close
items.why: The index is now only 0.95% above its 2025 close, so the year's gains are nearly gone and the next test is whether the 6,900 area holds on a retest.

items.why: A close below that level would confirm a 20% drawdown from the Oct 6 record, which tends to change positioning rules for trend-following funds.

items.headline: S&P 500 rebounded 4.7% on Nov 23 to 7,237; VIX fell from 35.9 to 26.6
items.why: A one-day bounce of this size after an 8.6% weekly drop is a volatility reset, not yet a confirmed low, until the index holds above Friday's close.
